activity.title: I am excited to share that my students’ paper, Evaluating Large Language Models in Undergraduate Mathematics: Balancing Potentials and Pitfalls, was accepted for publication in the ACM Journal on Responsible Computing! They took a class project and adapted it into a publication-worthy work as just sophomores in college! I am so so proud of them all - congrats Tanish Anandababu , Raghav Thind , Aatish Gupta , and Gourav Korada!!! https://lnkd.in/eGBRwuBc ...more ...more

I’ve been working towards AGI my whole life and I believe it is now close at hand. It’s critical that as a society we get the next steps right to ensure this profound technology benefits all of humanity and ushers in an incredible new age of discovery and wonder. As we enter this pivotal moment, I’ve decided to step into a new role as Chair of Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet Inc. This will allow me to focus on long-term AGI strategy and accelerating scientific breakthroughs, including leaning even further into my work at Isomorphic Labs where we are making extremely rapid and promising progress on our mission to cure disease. We’ve achieved so many extraordinary things at Google DeepMind so far and I’m very excited for this next chapter under the leadership of koray kavukcuoglu . I look forward to continuing to work with him, Sundar and the executive team. More details in our blog post: https://lnkd.in/eEdesa-X

Wish I could have turned back the wheel of time to see all those smiles at Google DeepMind. That was Jul 17, 2024, we were competing at the International Math Olympiad (IMO) for the very first time (using AI). I was presenting to GDM leadership (Demis, Koray, Jeff, Oriol, Ed, Quoc) at the "command center" in Mountain View, together with colleagues on the call from London. The screen was about how our AlphaGeometry2 solved IMO problem #4 in 19s in an elegant way. Not sure why we laughed so much, but I guess that doesn't matter. Just a beautiful memory :) This photo is to remember a remarkable chapter of Google DeepMind & I guess we will all keep marching forward, towards AGI, just not together. Regardless, I hope everyone doesn't forget that the ultimate goal is to benefit humanity & to quote our friend Po-Shen Loh: we should always find joy in working with one another! In the rare case you don't know why I have this post, see https://lnkd.in/gXEAEmNA for some context and more photos.

I dropped out of Georgia Tech and left my Google & Amazon internships to go all in on my startup. 🇵🇪 Dialogus is now backed by Y Combinator . We’re building the infrastructure layer for voice AI agents in enterprise. I was one semester away from graduating. However, the last few years taught me that growth sometimes asks you to leave behind what you know. If you’re building in voice AI, frontier models for real-time agents or in enterprise automation, I’d love to connect! #YCombinator #Peru #Startups #PeruAbroad

Pleased to share that our research using ML to infer heart rate from passive videos taken on smartphone front facing cameras, was just published at #Nature . It's been more than 10 years since I first saw research in this space (and that website is still up! https://lnkd.in/gyn9erRV ) Here we demonstrated accuracy across a range of conditions spanning both lab and 'free-living' study conditions, and across skin tone subgroups as characterized using spectrometers.
